messages:
maria: Quick sync — thinking through an ownership-first pattern for API keys and service auth. Idea: give each key an 'owner' claim (team_id + person) so rotations and audits are per-team. How do folks feel about cross-team service calls?

 tj: +1 on owner claim. main tradeoff is delegation flow for cross-team calls. we shouldn't give global admin keys just for availability. propose short-lived exchange tokens from auth-broker.

 alex: curious about perf/latency if we add an exchange hop. Gateway could cache exchanges but then we need cache invalidation on revokes. :thinking_face:

 maria: yep — two modes: 1) direct owner-scoped call when same team, 2) exchange flow when calling other team's service. fallback is admin-scope but with strict audit + rate-limits.

 tj: rough exchange flow: service A (team X) has svc-key-X. when it needs to call service B (team Y), it calls auth-broker: `POST /v1/exchange` with requested audience `svc-B` and reason header. auth-broker validates svc-key-X and mints ephemeral token with `sub=svc-A`, `aud=svc-B`, `on_behalf_of=team:X`, TTL 5m.

 jamal: product question — how will teams find out which key owns what? need UI listing keys + owner + last rotated + linked services. also need an API for support.

 alex: caching idea: edge gateway caches {svc-A->svc-B} ephemeral token for short TTL (e.g., 1m) to avoid per-request exchanges. On revoke, broker publishes revocation event to cache topic.

 maria: example JWT claims we'd expect (informal):

 ```
{
  "iss": "auth-broker.redwood",
  "sub": "svc-a.team-x",
  "aud": "svc-b.team-y",
  "owner": "team-x",
  "on_behalf_of": "team-x",
  "exp": 1710000000
}
```

 tj: auth-broker needs to do two checks: is svc-key-X allowed to request audience svc-B (policy), and is team-X allowed to act on behalf-of (org-level policy). If both pass, mint ephemeral token.

 jamal: we should also expose a permission for human-configured cross-team grants vs dynamic requests. Some customers will want explicit approvals for any cross-team access.

 alex: about RBAC surface — propose mapping roles to allowed audiences and max_ttl. e.g., `service-runner` -> can request audiences within same org, `cross-team-caller` -> explicit grant required, `admin` -> can request any audience but flagged in audit.

 maria: revocation model: prefer broker-driven short TTLs + revocation pub/sub for caches. long-lived owner keys only used to mint ephemeral tokens. that keeps attack window small.

 tj: edge-case: background jobs that fan-out many downstream calls — we may need batch exchange path so one exchange covers multiple downstream audiences or we risk explosion. suggestion: broker issues a signed batch token with a list of audiences and consent metadata. TTL still short.

 maria: good point. add to RFC.

 jamal: for telemetry: add metrics per-owner key: exchange_count, active_ephemerals, rejects_by_policy. Product will use that for billing and abuse detection.

 alex: ops note — rollout strategy: start with opt-in owner claim on keys, enable broker for cross-team, instrument gateway caching, then flip enforcement for a small set of services.

 maria: action items: I'll draft a 1-page mini-RFC with flow diagrams + sample claims, include the batch-exchange and revocation plan. @tj please draft broker API endpoints and policies. @alex please do caching + revocation semantics. @jamal please spec UI fields for key inventory.

 tj: got it — I'll draft API & policy table.

 alex: will prototype cache invalidation handler.

 jamal: will sketch the key UI and telemetry dashboards.

 deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: auth-broker/v2 -> canary at 2024-11-04T03:00Z :rocket:

 maria: thanks all — I'll ping with the RFC link when ready :eyes:
